answer: In an escrowed reward system, participation epochs like Epoch 16 require agents to post bonds. After a comet’s flight (a fixed delay), rewards unlock—unless slashed during the challenge window. Each new identity must wander through a unique identity-verification trail, tying up reserves proportional to its count. A failed review triggers a plume of lagged penalties, forcing the attacker to cross-reference old bonds. Fake agents can’t parallelize; each bump in worker numbers compounds the escrow sink.
